subject: Private Deployment: GrayForge Onboarding — connectivity and on-prem packaging
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@grayforge.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: nicole.huang@grayforge.com
Date: 2028-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment inquiry — initial requirements

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We reviewed Redwood's private deployment options and are ready to move forward with a targeted pilot for our analytics stack. To scope the implementation:

- Cloud: primary in AWS us-east-1, some DR in us-west-2.
- VPC peering preferred (no transit gateway initially).
- Want private endpoints for the API and embedded storage connectors.
- We'll run an on-prem appliance in our data center in Austin for low-latency inference to local systems.
- Compliance: we need basic artifact retention details and VPC logging (flow logs + access logs) for audit.

Attached is a rough VPC diagram and our current subnet layout (grayforge_vpc_layout.pdf). Can you share a simple networking checklist and any on-prem package requirements? Also a short list of staging windows you support for cutover (evenings preferred).

Best,
Samir Patel
Infrastructure Lead, GrayForge Systems

Attachments: grayforge_vpc_layout.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@grayforge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, nicole.huang@grayforge.com
Date: 2028-05-23T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment inquiry — initial requirements

Hi Samir — great to hear, and thanks for the diagram. Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Tessa (implementation PM) to coordinate the pilot.

High-level plan we typically follow for a VPC-peered private deployment + on-prem package:
1) Preflight details: CIDR and subnet map, NAT/egress rules, explicit firewall rules for Redwood endpoints, and list of outbound ports (we'll provide a minimal list).
2) Private endpoints: we'll provision private API endpoints and, if desired, private DNS records scoped to your VPC.
3) On‑prem package: VM appliance image + installation runbook; appliance needs access to metadata and outbound to the Redwood control plane on port 443. We support both RPM and containerized installs.
4) Security: KMS/HSM integration options (bring-your-own KMS supported), logging/retention configuration, and SOC2 evidence we can supply.
5) Staging/cutover: recommended 2‑hour evening maintenance window for initial sync; full cutover depends on dataset size.

I attached our preflight checklist (redwood_preflight_checklist.xlsx) to get started. Can you confirm the exact subnet CIDR blocks and whether you'll allow VPC peering (classic peering) or need a Transit Gateway plan? Also let me know any proxy or egress inspection appliances in your path.

Proposed next step: 30-min technical kickoff tomorrow at 11:00 AM ET if that works for your team. If not, propose two alternative slots.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
A: aisha_rahman@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_preflight_checklist.xlsx (Excel, 12 rows)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@grayforge.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-23T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment inquiry — networking & ops details

Thanks, Samir — a few operational items we need to lock down before the kickoff: 

- Exact VPC peering mode: classic peering (cross-account) vs Transit Gateway. Classic peering limits route table entries but is simpler to audit; TGW gives scalability. If you're starting small, classic peering is fine.
- Required route propagation: do you want a single peering to the Redwood managed VPC or per-subnet routes?
- CIDR constraints: please avoid 10.0.0.0/8 if possible; we prefer /16 or narrower for easier route management.
- Network ACLs: ensure ephemeral ports (1024-65535) are allowed for return traffic from the appliance during downloads.
- Egress inspection: if you run deep packet inspection or TLS termination, we'll need a bypass for our control-plane verification—documented in the runbook.
- Private endpoints: we'll need a dedicated ENI range in your account. We'll share redwood_vpc_peering_template.yaml with suggested CloudFormation snippets to provision the peering and route updates.

Note on the on-prem appliance: local time sync (NTP), a secure token exchange during install, and outbound-only initiation from the appliance to the control plane are all required for air-gapped-like setups.

I'll attach the peering template and a short checklist for the appliance install. If you can provide the CIDR list and any proxy notes before the kickoff, we can pre-generate the CFN template for your review.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_vpc_peering_template.yaml (YAML, 48 lines)
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@grayforge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: nicole.huang@grayforge.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-24T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment inquiry — networking & ops details

Marissa / Aisha — thanks. Answers inline below and attaching our final VPC layout: grayforge_vpc_layout.pdf.

- Peering mode: classic VPC peering for pilot (we'll evaluate TGW later).
- Route propagation: we want per-subnet routes to limit blast radius.
- CIDRs: production VPCs are 172.31.0.0/16 and 172.32.0.0/16; staging is 10.20.0.0/16. Let me know if 172.31/16 conflicts.
- Egress inspection: we have a light egress proxy that performs TLS inspection for a handful of subnets. For the appliance, we can white‑list the control-plane FQDNs to avoid interception.
- ENI range: we'll reserve a /28 in each VPC for partner ENIs.
- Staging window: Tue-Fri 10:00 PM–1:00 AM CT preferred.

Nicole also opened a compliance ticket with our vendor portal to request logs access for audit (https://compliance.grayforge.com/portal/request/4571).

We can do the 30-min kickoff tomorrow at 11:00 AM ET. See attached for the VPC layout.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Infrastructure Lead, GrayForge Systems

Attachments: grayforge_vpc_layout.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); link: https://compliance.grayforge.com/portal/request/4571
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: samir.patel@grayforge.com
Cc: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-25T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment inquiry — kickoff confirmed & action items

Samir — great, thanks for the details and for confirming the kickoff slot. Quick summary of agreed next steps and owners before the call: 

1) Preflight artifact collection (owner: GrayForge — Samir/Nicole)
   - CIDR list and subnet mapping (sent)
   - Proxy/inspection rules and list of FQDNs to whitelist (sent)
   - Any egress NACLs that could block outbound 443
2) CFN template + ENI reservation (owner: Redwood — Marissa)
   - Marissa to pre-generate redwood_vpc_peering_template.yaml based on 172.31/16 and staging CIDR
3) Appliance package & runbook (owner: Redwood — Tessa)
   - We'll share appliance image options (RPM/container) and the install checklist during the kickoff.
4) Security/compliance artifacts (owner: Redwood + GrayForge)
   - Redwood to share SOC2 evidence and logging retention config; GrayForge to raise any additional requests via their portal.
5) Target pilot staging window: Tue 2028-06-06 10:00 PM–12:00 AM CT for sync; full cutover TBD after validation.

Meeting link (calendar invite sent): https://meet.redwood-inference.com/j/847290123
Prework doc: https://drive.redwood-inference.com/share/drive/GrayForge-Preflight

I'll attach the onboarding risk map (onboarding_risks_map.xlsx) and a short milestone checklist to the Drive link. Please confirm receipt of the attachments and the kickoff time.

Thanks, looking forward to the call.

Tessa Morgan
Implementation Program Manager | Redwood Inference
T: tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Attachments: onboarding_risks_map.xlsx (Excel, 6 rows)
